messages:
lucy: Heads-up - observed progressive quality drift on the fp8->int4 cascade for the suggestions model during the canary window. attaching short diffs.

mike: saw the diff. per-token log-prob diverges starting ~token 420, downstream rank flips increase.

raj: reproduced on a small local run. hypothesis: headwise scale clipping + density-adaptive quant profile causes late-context amplification. kv cache looks fine.

mina: which quant profile landed? we recently tried `density-savings-3` on non-critical tenants.

lucy: yes that profile was used for the canary cohort. it's more aggressive in tail bins.

mike: quick numbers: avg cost savings ~18%, P95 latency +2ms, but late-token NLL +0.25 on longctx eval.

raj: suggestion: short-term runtime guard: if `deg_metric > 0.6` or `head_saturation_pct > 30` then fallback to fp8 for remainder of request. keep it opt-in via header.

mina: agree. we need trace fields for that: `precision_degradation`, `head_saturation_pct`, `cache_hit_rate`. make them optional to avoid overhead.

lucy: runtime API sketch: client sends `X-Precision-Guard: longctx-fallback` and server can return `X-Precision-Guard-Activated: 1` when it flips. also support query `?trace_precision=1` for opt-in telemetry.

mike: implementation note: fallback mid-request requires hot-swap of kernel path. runtime already supports switching quant kernels at slice boundaries but we must preserve KV alignment. risky but doable.

raj: long-term: we should refactor profile selection into a precision-adapter layer that evaluates per-request signal and picks quant profile before execution. keeps decision logic out of core runtime.

mina: that adapter could also surface a confidence score and a safe_fallback_profile to simplify ops. good decoupling.

canary-bot: alert: longctx-guard triggered on 2 canary shards (eu-central-1). Canary rate limited.

lucy: action list: 1) implement opt-in trace fields (mina) 2) add header-driven guard prototype (mike) 3) run targeted shadow comparing aggressive vs conservative profiles on longctx eval set (raj) 4) draft RFC for precision-adapter refactor (lucy).

mike: rough cost calc: enabling guard on all longctx requests increases infra tokens ~12% in sims. share with finance for quick check.

raj: I'll run shadow tonight with three arms: (A) full-prec baseline (B) fp8->int4 aggressive (C) aggressive + fallback-to-fp8-after-420-tokens. will post metrics (BLEU, NLL, rank-flips).

mina: i'll add `?trace_precision=1` to the trace pipeline and ensure it's off by default. add unit tests for payload shape.

lucy: if shadows show statistically significant late-token regressions we'll pause the aggressive profile for the external tenant cohort and initiate rollback playbook.

ops-bot: reminder: escalation channel #eng-oncall and incident runbook template available at https://intra/redwood/playbooks/precision-fallback.

lucy: thanks all. will collect the shadow outputs and start RFC draft tomorrow.
